facts.statement: The genus Alligatorellus was described by Gervais in 1871.
The type species of the genus is Alligatorellus beaumonti.
A skeleton of Alligatorellus was found in the Solnhofen Limestone of Kelheim, Germany.
facts.quote: A skeleton of Alligatorellus has also been found in the Solnhofen Limestone of Kelheim, Germany.

facts.statement: The German skeleton was likely washed into a lagoon within a marine environment before fossilization.
facts.quote: The limestone was deposited in a marine environment and the individual may have washed into a lagoon where it was fossilized.

facts.statement: The German skeleton preserves osteoderms and limb bones in three dimensions.
facts.quote: The skeleton includes osteoderms and limb bones, which are three-dimensionally preserved.

facts.statement: The German skeleton provides more anatomical detail than most other atoposaurid fossils because it is three-dimensional rather than compressed flat.
facts.quote: The German skeleton shows more details of atoposaurid anatomy than most fossils, as other atoposaurid remains are compressed flat.

facts.statement: Alligatorellus belongs to the family Atoposauridae.
Alligatorellus lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages, between 154.8 and 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 145.06 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Alligatorellus is an extinct genus of atoposaurid crocodyliform related to Atoposaurus.
rejected.quote: Alligatorellus is an extinct genus of atoposaurid crocodyliform found in France that was related to Atoposaurus.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Alligatorellus is an extinct genus of atoposaurid crocodyliform'

rejected.statement: Remains of four crinoids that lived in the lagoon were found in the same fossil block as the Alligatorellus skeleton.
rejected.quote: Remains of four crinoids that lived in the lagoon are found in the same block as the skeleton.
